account_scenarios.intro: I keep forgetting to pay my bill. Can you set it up so it gets paid automatically?

body.speaker: agent
body.text: Yes, that's called AutoPay, and it's free. I'm looking at your account and it's turned off right now. Your current bill, {bill_amount}, is due on {statement_date}.

body.speaker: customer
body.text: That's the one I'm afraid I'll miss.

body.speaker: agent
body.text: There's a Visa saved on the account from your last payment. Would you like AutoPay to use that card?

body.speaker: customer
body.text: Yes, use that one.

body.speaker: agent
body.text: Okay, I've turned AutoPay on. It will charge that card on the due date each month, starting with this bill.

body.speaker: customer
body.text: And if I get a new card?

body.speaker: agent
body.text: You can change it in the My Northline app under Billing, then Payment methods. Just do it at least 2 days before the due date.

body.speaker: customer
body.text: Good. One less thing to remember.

account_scenarios.intro: I won't be able to pay my bill on time this month. My pension check is coming late.

body.speaker: agent
body.text: I understand, and thank you for calling before the due date. I have your account open: {bill_amount} is due on {statement_date}.

body.speaker: customer
body.text: That's right. I can pay it about a week after that.

body.speaker: agent
body.text: What you want is a payment arrangement. It can give you up to 14 extra days, but our billing team has to approve it.

body.speaker: customer
body.text: Can you ask them for me?

body.speaker: agent
body.text: Yes. I've put the request on your account and sent it over. Your reference number is {ticket}.

body.speaker: customer
body.text: How will I know if they said yes?

body.speaker: agent
body.text: They'll text you at {phone}, and the new due date will show in the My Northline app.

body.speaker: customer
body.text: All right. Thank you for being kind about it.

account_scenarios.intro: I can make calls fine, but I haven't gotten a single text message in three days.

body.speaker: agent
body.text: Let's sort that out. What kind of phone are you using?

body.speaker: customer
body.text: A {device}.

body.speaker: agent
body.text: Thanks. I'm looking at your line now, and I can see a text messaging block was switched on for it three days ago.

body.speaker: customer
body.text: A block? I never asked for that.

body.speaker: agent
body.text: It may have been tapped by accident in the app. I've removed the block from your line just now. Please turn the phone off and back on.

body.speaker: customer
body.text: Okay, give me a second... oh, here they come. A whole bunch of them.

body.speaker: agent
body.text: Good. If it ever happens again, call us back and we'll check the line for you.

body.speaker: customer
body.text: I will. Thank you.

account_scenarios.intro: My grandson says my new phone doesn't need a SIM card. Can you switch me over to that eSIM thing?

body.speaker: agent
body.text: I can. I see the {device} on your account, and it does support eSIM. Your line is on a plastic SIM card right now.

body.speaker: customer
body.text: Is there a charge for changing?

body.speaker: agent
body.text: No, eSIM is free. I'm sending the eSIM to your phone now. You'll need to be on Wi-Fi.

body.speaker: customer
body.text: I'm on my home Wi-Fi.

body.speaker: agent
body.text: Good. A message should pop up saying a cellular plan is ready to install. Tap it, then tap Continue.

body.speaker: customer
body.text: Nothing has popped up. I've been staring at it.

body.speaker: agent
body.text: Sometimes it takes a while. I've left your plastic SIM active on the account, so you still have service. If nothing shows up within the hour, restart the phone and call us back.

body.speaker: customer
body.text: All right. I'll keep an eye on it.

account_scenarios.intro: My laptop stopped connecting through my phone. I think I ran out of that hotspot data.

body.speaker: agent
body.text: You did. I can see on your account that the hotspot allowance on {plan_name} is used up for this month, and you've used {data_used} overall.

body.speaker: customer
body.text: Can I get more? I need the laptop for my church newsletter.

body.speaker: agent
body.text: You can add Hotspot Boost. It's $10 a month for 10 GB of hotspot data, and you can take it off any time.

body.speaker: customer
body.text: Please add it.

body.speaker: agent
body.text: It's added to your line. It will show as Hotspot Boost, $10, on your next bill. Try the laptop again in a minute or two.

body.speaker: customer
body.text: It's connecting now. Thank you.

account_scenarios.intro: I just got back from visiting my daughter in {country} and there are charges on my bill I don't recognize.

body.speaker: agent
body.text: Welcome back. Let me look at the bill. I see the statement dated {statement_date} came to {bill_amount}, and it includes the International Day Pass on six days.

body.speaker: customer
body.text: Six? I only turned the phone on a few times.

body.speaker: agent
body.text: The pass is $10 for each day the phone is used abroad, even for one text. Your usage shows activity on six different days.

body.speaker: customer
body.text: I'm sure it was five. I kept it in the hotel safe on the last day.

body.speaker: agent
body.text: Then you can dispute that day. I can't change the charge myself, so I've opened a dispute on your account for the billing team. The reference is {ticket}.

body.speaker: customer
body.text: How long does that take?

body.speaker: agent
body.text: They review it in 3 to 5 business days and let you know the result. Please keep paying the rest of the bill in the meantime.

body.speaker: customer
body.text: Okay. I'll wait to hear.

account_scenarios.intro: I reported my phone lost last week, and wouldn't you know it, it was in my coat pocket the whole time. Can you turn it back on?

body.speaker: agent
body.text: I'm glad it turned up. Yes, I can see the line was suspended and the device was blocked on your account last week.

body.speaker: customer
body.text: So it's no use to me until you fix that?

body.speaker: agent
body.text: Right. I'm lifting the suspension now, and I've taken the block off the {device}.

body.speaker: customer
body.text: Do I need a new SIM card?

body.speaker: agent
body.text: No, the one inside is still good. Turn the phone off, wait 30 seconds, and turn it on again.

body.speaker: customer
body.text: It says Northline at the top now.

body.speaker: agent
body.text: Then you're back in service on {phone}. Nothing else on the account changed while it was suspended.

body.speaker: customer
body.text: Thank goodness. Thank you.

account_scenarios.intro: I spend the winter with my sister overseas and I don't use this phone there. Can I stop the service for a while without losing my number?

body.speaker: agent
body.text: Yes. Anyone can pause service for up to 90 days in a 12-month period and keep the number. When would you like it to start?

body.speaker: customer
body.text: The first of next month, for about two months.

body.speaker: agent
body.text: Okay. I've set a pause on your line starting on the 1st, for 60 days. It's noted on your account under {ticket}.

body.speaker: customer
body.text: Will the phone work at all while I'm gone?

body.speaker: agent
body.text: No calls, texts or data while it's paused, except 911. Your number, {phone}, stays yours.

body.speaker: customer
body.text: And when I come home?

body.speaker: agent
body.text: It switches back on by itself when the 60 days are up. If you're back early, call us and we'll end the pause that day.

body.speaker: customer
body.text: That's just what I needed.

account_scenarios.intro: I can't read my bill anymore. The print is so small I need a magnifying glass.

body.speaker: agent
body.text: We can fix that. Large-print bills are free. I see you get a paper bill mailed to {address}. Is that still where it should go?

body.speaker: customer
body.text: Yes, that's my address.

body.speaker: agent
body.text: I've changed your bill format to large print. The next statement, the one after {statement_date}, will come that way.

body.speaker: customer
body.text: Does that cost more than the regular paper one?

body.speaker: agent
body.text: No. Large print itself is free. The paper bill is still $2 a month, same as you pay now.

body.speaker: customer
body.text: That's fine. I like having paper.

body.speaker: agent
body.text: If you ever want a person to go through the bill with you, call 611 and we'll read it line by line.

body.speaker: customer
body.text: I may take you up on that.

account_scenarios.intro: I got a message saying my number is being moved to a new SIM card. I didn't ask for that. Is someone stealing my number?

body.speaker: agent
body.text: I understand why that's frightening. I've checked your account, and there is no SIM change and no transfer request on your number. Nothing has been moved.

body.speaker: customer
body.text: So the message was a fake?

body.speaker: agent
body.text: It looks that way. Did it ask you to click anything or call a number?

body.speaker: customer
body.text: It had a link. I didn't touch it.

body.speaker: agent
body.text: Good. To be safe, I've turned on Number Lock for your line. While it's on, your number can't be moved to another SIM or another company.

body.speaker: customer
body.text: Does that cost anything?

body.speaker: agent
body.text: No, it's free. You can see it in the My Northline app under Security. And you can forward that message to 7726 so it gets reported.

body.speaker: customer
body.text: I'll do that right now. Thank you.

general_scenarios.intro: My calls keep breaking up when I'm inside my house. Out in the yard they're fine.

body.speaker: agent
body.text: That usually means the walls are blocking the signal. It happens in a lot of homes. Do you have Wi-Fi in the house?

body.speaker: customer
body.text: Yes, my grandson set it up for my tablet.

body.speaker: agent
body.text: Then Wi-Fi calling should help. The phone makes calls over your home internet instead of the tower. What phone do you have?

body.speaker: customer
body.text: It's a {device}.

body.speaker: agent
body.text: Open Settings, tap Phone or Calls, then tap Wi-Fi Calling and switch it on.

body.speaker: customer
body.text: It's asking me for an address.

body.speaker: agent
body.text: That's the emergency address, so 911 knows where you are. Type in your home address there. It's saved on the phone itself.

body.speaker: customer
body.text: Done. It says Wi-Fi Calling at the top now.

body.speaker: agent
body.text: Good. Calls you make inside the house will go over the Wi-Fi from now on, and it doesn't cost anything extra.

body.speaker: customer
body.text: I'll try it tonight. Thank you.

general_scenarios.intro: Some number keeps calling me about a car warranty, four or five times a day. How do I make it stop?

body.speaker: agent
body.text: You can block that number right on your phone. Open the Phone app and tap Recents.

body.speaker: customer
body.text: Okay, I see the list of calls.

body.speaker: agent
body.text: Find one of those calls, tap the little i next to it, and choose Block number.

body.speaker: customer
body.text: It's asking if I'm sure. Yes. All right, it's blocked.

body.speaker: agent
body.text: There's also Northline Call Filter. It's free for everyone, and it labels likely spam calls on the screen. You turn it on in the My Northline app, under Security.

body.speaker: customer
body.text: Do you have to do something on my account for that?

body.speaker: agent
body.text: No, I don't need to go into your account at all. It's a switch in the app that you turn on yourself.

body.speaker: customer
body.text: Good. I'll have my daughter show me.

general_scenarios.intro: My daughter put the My Northline app on my phone. How do I look at my bill on it?

body.speaker: agent
body.text: It's just a couple of taps. Open the app and tap Billing. The most recent bill is at the top of the list.

body.speaker: customer
body.text: And what am I looking at when it opens?

body.speaker: agent
body.text: Every bill has four parts: plan charges, add-ons, one-time fees and taxes. The due date is printed there too. It's always 21 days after the statement date.

body.speaker: customer
body.text: Can you tell me what mine says?

body.speaker: agent
body.text: Not right now. I haven't opened your account on this call, and I'd need to verify you first. But the app will show you the same thing I would see.

body.speaker: customer
body.text: No, that's all right. I just wanted to know where to look.

body.speaker: agent
body.text: Then you're set. If the app ever asks you to sign in, use the Forgot password link and it will text you a code.

body.speaker: customer
body.text: I'll give it a try this afternoon.

general_scenarios.intro: My neighbor is thinking about switching to Northline and asked me what your plans cost. Can you go over them so I can tell her?

body.speaker: agent
body.text: Happy to. The price list is the same for everyone. Does she mostly call and text, or does she use the internet on her phone?

body.speaker: customer
body.text: Mostly calls. A little email.

body.speaker: agent
body.text: Then there's Northline Talk at $15 a month, which is talk and text with no data, or Northline Starter 1 at $20 with 1 GB for email and maps.

body.speaker: customer
body.text: What if she wants to watch videos?

body.speaker: agent
body.text: Northline Extra 20 is $45 a month with 20 GB. The unlimited plans start at $50 a month for Northline Unlimited Essentials.

body.speaker: customer
body.text: Is there a contract? She got burned by one before.

body.speaker: agent
body.text: No contracts and no early termination fee on any plan. There is a one-time Activation Fee of $35 for a new line.

body.speaker: customer
body.text: I'll write that down for her. Thank you.

general_scenarios.intro: My eyes are getting worse and my niece says the phone can read the screen out loud. How do I turn that on?

body.speaker: agent
body.text: It can. That feature is called a screen reader. What kind of phone do you have?

body.speaker: customer
body.text: It's a {device}.

body.speaker: agent
body.text: Okay. Open Settings and tap Accessibility. On an iPhone you'll see VoiceOver, and on an Android phone it's called TalkBack. Tap it and switch it on.

body.speaker: customer
body.text: Oh! It's talking to me.

body.speaker: agent
body.text: That's it working. Now you touch something once to hear it, and tap twice to open it.

body.speaker: customer
body.text: That will take some getting used to.

body.speaker: agent
body.text: It does for everybody. It also works inside the My Northline app, so the phone can read a bill or a usage screen out loud to you.

body.speaker: customer
body.text: Isn't that something. Thank you.

general_scenarios.intro: How do I get my tablet on the internet through my phone? We're going up to the lake and there's no Wi-Fi there.

body.speaker: agent
body.text: You'd use the phone as a hotspot. It shares the phone's data with the tablet. On the phone, open Settings and look for Hotspot and tethering.

body.speaker: customer
body.text: I found it.

body.speaker: agent
body.text: Turn on Wi-Fi hotspot, then choose a password of at least 8 characters. On the tablet, pick the phone's name from the Wi-Fi list and type that password.

body.speaker: customer
body.text: Will that cost me extra?

body.speaker: agent
body.text: That depends on the plan a person has. Hotspot data comes out of a separate allowance. Northline Plus 10 includes 2 GB of it, for example, and Northline Talk includes none.

body.speaker: customer
body.text: How do I know what I have?

body.speaker: agent
body.text: The quickest way is the My Northline app. Tap Usage and it shows your hotspot data. Or text the word USAGE to 611 and you get a free reply.

body.speaker: customer
body.text: I'll check before we leave. Thanks.
